items.title: 1.9 Trends in bonding in the oxides and chlorides of period 3

source_refs.note: Topic 1.9, printed page 16: the ionic-to-covalent trend in period 3 oxides and chlorides. The print numbers the groups 1 to 7 in the old style.

blocks.text: The oxides of groups 1, 2 and 3, for example Na2O, have more ionic character: they exist as giant ionic lattices with strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions. The oxides of groups 4 to 7, for example SO2, are more covalent and exist as covalent molecules with weak intermolecular forces. The transition results from the increasing electronegativity and decreasing ionic character along the period.

Similarly the chlorides of groups 1, 2 and 3, for example NaCl, are predominantly ionic, while the chlorides of the elements of groups 4 to 7, for example PCl5, are covalent. The covalent character of the chlorides increases because the difference in electronegativity between the halogen and the other atom decreases.
